boundary: Pass 6136's monotonicity rests on alpha at q = 7 and 11, which are ILS PLATEAUS not proofs -- though the method reproduced both proved values at q = 3 and 5 (Pass 6048). Pass 6138 is a NEGATIVE: no substrate-internal distinguisher between U and U* was found, and that is a finding rather than an incomplete search

pass_6136_characteristic_3_is_an_output.caveat: q = 7 and 11 are unproved plateaus; the monotonicity is credible but not proved, and proving alpha(W(3,7)) would settle it
pass_6136_characteristic_3_is_an_output.finding: efficiency DECREASES monotonically. Among all q supporting chirality, q = 3 is the CLOSEST to admitting an ovoid -- the least defective chirality-bearing symplectic space
pass_6136_characteristic_3_is_an_output.the_consequence: this selects q = 3 WITHOUT ASSUMING characteristic 3. Characteristic 3 is an OUTPUT of the selection, not an input to it -- which removes the last unexplained input Pass 6131 listed
pass_6136_characteristic_3_is_an_output.the_measure: chirality-supporting q are odd, hence have NO ovoid, so alpha falls short of q^2+1. The efficiency alpha/(q^2+1) measures how close the space comes to admitting one anyway
pass_6136_characteristic_3_is_an_output.the_question: chirality needs q = 3 mod 4, giving {3, 7, 11, 19, 23, 27, 31, ...}. Nothing in that condition mentions characteristic 3. So what picks 3?

candidates_checked: F_3* = {1,2}: its unique nontrivial element is canonical, but it lives in F_3, not in the character field, and supplies no cube root
Frobenius x -> x^3: acts TRIVIALLY on F_3, so it makes no choice either
pass_6138_the_distinguisher_is_not_there.verdict: NO substrate-internal distinguisher found. The gap named at Pass 6106 remains open
pass_6138_the_distinguisher_is_not_there.what_is_needed: the character field is Q(sqrt(-3)) = Q(omega). Swapping U and U* is complex conjugation, which exchanges omega and omega-bar. So a substrate-internal distinguisher must canonically pick ONE primitive cube root of unity
pass_6138_the_distinguisher_is_not_there.why_this_is_a_finding: the obstruction is now located precisely -- it is not that the substrate lacks a complex structure (Pass 353 gave one) nor that it can undo it (Pass 6096 forbade that), but that nothing inside F_3 selects a cube root of unity. That is a sharper statement of what is missing than 'chirality is unselectable'

pass_6139_the_arc_in_full.ends_at: a canonical pair with no internal way to choose a member, because nothing in F_3 picks a cube root of unity
pass_6139_the_arc_in_full.started: Pass 346: chirality is unselectable from inside the substrate
steps: Sp(4,3) is PERFECT, so it cannot swap half-spins (Pass 6096)
20 of its 34 characters are non-self-dual, including both Weil constituents (Pass 6104)
so a canonical unswappable PAIR exists
that requires q = 3 mod 4, NOT characteristic 3 -- q = 9 has none (Pass 6120)
among characteristic-3 options q = 3, 27, 243 are identical, so minimality picks 3 (Pass 6128)
and among ALL chirality-supporting q, q = 3 maximises efficiency, so characteristic 3 is an output not an input (this pass)
pass_6139_the_arc_in_full.what_that_is_worth: the no-go moved from 'the substrate cannot pose the question' to 'the substrate poses it canonically and cannot answer it'. The remaining gap is one specific missing choice, not a structural impossibility
